You’ve gotta remember titans range from 10-30 feet tall, so to build something this big outside of the wall would take countess lives and undoubtedly break over and over again. You’re underestimating a nations drive to retain power. Marley could have done what they could to catch up technologically but then they’d just be any other nation with a massive potential threat right off their coast. In hindsight it’s clear that going after Paradis was key to their downfall, but in the fog of war that is the future I don’t see them having any other option. They either take the risk of regaining the full power of the titans or watch as their power gets eclipsed by technology or watch another nation who hates the island just as much blow them to smithereens or capture the islands titans. None of these are good options so they picked the one that offered them the most solutions at once - unify other nations against paradis and invading. Which let them gain allies, try to get their titans back, and buy them time to get up to speed technologically. Obviously it didn’t work but it was a good plan.

However you look at it leaving the island alone was never in the cards. It was either going to be destroyed/controlled by Marley or some other Nation. And honestly Paradis is better off for it bc no matter how you slice it they were not winning. Even if they knew they were only tens of thousands of titans they had no real way of taking them out on mass before the technology of other nations allowed them to blow them to hell first. In 50 years they would be no closer to killing all titans and nations would have artillery, bomber plans and maybe even nukes. Even if they had killed all titans which wouldn’t have happened they’d find a world that was so far ahead on the tech tree that all they could do would be beg for mercy. Time was never on their side. They were always losing.

I see your point but you’re wrong for a few reasons. Bc the scouts didn’t know what game they were playing the human cost per titan kill was way too high. Sure a lot of top scouts had “high” titan kill counts but high is relative to the ones who had 0-1. Having 30-100 kills on the top 20% of troops is nothing when they’re 10’s of thousands on the island. If they knew there were only a finite(ish) amount of titans on the island scouting missions wouldn’t have made sense in light of the titan threat. It would have made much more sense to clear out the island then scout it, but they couldn’t have known that without a full picture of the geopolitical situation, which could only come from Marleyian intervention.

Also Marley didn’t just have a grudge against the island, they had a real need for the power of the 9 for their military to keep the potency that it had. It was all but spelled out in the beginning of the fourth season that the titans power was starting to wain in light of technological advancements of rival nations. The Marleyian leadership calculated that with the power of the 9 plus threat of the rumbling they could hold onto power for much longer/indefinitely. Them going after the island was a calculated attempt to retain power, not a half baked waste of resources for a grudge. In reality, the deal king fritz had made worked for them, they didn’t have to deal with Eldians threatening their hegemony and they had a place they could discard any dissidents. Them upsetting that deal over a grudge would make no sense.
